Notes: Dhakal p. 49 prints /anike/ “to bring”. Turner1174 section 1 gives Pali āneti “brings, fetches”, Bhojpuri ānal, Old Awadhi ānab and Hindi ānnā. The Darai -ike is the ordinary infinitive suffix, illustrated in the source morphology. The nonlong a is consistent with the source statement that vowel length is not distinctive. Darai source-backed verb and ordinal batch; autonomous continuation.

Dhakal pp. 45 and 51 print /pʰerike/ “to change” in minimal pairs. Turner9078 section 2 is transitive *phērayati; it specifically lists Nepali phernu “to change” and Old Awadhi pheraï “turns, changes”. This contrasts with the separate Darai /pʰorike/ “to break”. Darai source-backed verb and ordinal batch; autonomous continuation.

Dhakal pp. 53 and 67 print /tisrən/ “third” (the latter syllabified tis.rən). Turner6018 section 1 explicitly gives Tarai Nepali tisar and Awadhi tīsar “third”, alongside Hindi tīsrā; the Darai ending is retained without projecting an unattested ancestral suffix. Darai source-backed verb and ordinal batch; autonomous continuation.
